reply: {"action":"conclude","root_cause":"Shop purchases and buy pads are two separate purchase paths that do not share state. The shop path (UpgradeService) records ownership, but the pad system that owns the pad parts, labels and prices does not observe that ownership. A pad bought in the shop therefore keeps its label, price and touchable state. The reverse also fails: pads are not reconciled with ownership, so the two views drift apart. The earlier fix in UpgradeService alone was rejected because the pad side never re-reads ownership. I could not run probes before concluding, so this is inferred from the anomaly, the rejected fix and the file layout, not proven.","file":"ServerScriptService/Tycoon.luau","evidence":"No probes were run, so there is no direct evidence. The earlier UpgradeService-only fix was rejected, with the check still reporting 'no visible touchable Dropper 2 pad'. That suggests the pad state is owned and updated in the pad-building code, not in UpgradeService. Round 2 also showed bought pads keeping their label and price, which points the same way.","fix_hint":"In Tycoon.luau, make pad state a function of the player's owned upgrades. Add one refreshPad/applyOwnership routine that hides the pad and its BillboardGui label and price, and disables its touch, whenever the upgrade is owned. Call it from the pad purchase path, from the shop purchase path (via a callback or event fired by UpgradeService on success), and when the plot is claimed or loaded. Make a pad touch for an already-owned upgrade a no-op, and keep unowned pads visible and touchable."}
